grades.question: A Power's own threshold gives it +1 Range. If the threshold is met on both the original use and its Repeat, does the Repeat get +2 Range? If that threshold is no longer met on the Repeat, is the first +1 retained?

expected.answer: Do not stack the same internal Range boost a second time: the Repeat retains the original +1, not +2. It retains that Range modification even if the threshold is no longer met when repeating.

requested_parts: A Power's own threshold gives it +1 Range. If the threshold is met on both the original use and its Repeat, does the Repeat get +2 Range?
If that threshold is no longer met on the Repeat, is the first +1 retained?
observed.answer: No stack same Range bonus; +1 persists on Repeat even if threshold no longer met.

evidence.text:
- The **targeting Range box** gives the maximum land distance from **one of your Presence**. Range 0 requires your Presence in the target land. Origin icons may require your Sacred Site or Presence in a particular terrain.
- Target restrictions may specify terrain, Coastal/Inland, contents, or a Spirit. A slash between piece/terrain icons means either or both types, not an additional allowance for each.
- Unless explicitly different, use **one target land or Spirit, once per turn**. Multiple effects and all innate levels apply to that same target. You cannot pay twice for an ordinary card use or use an innate twice just by having twice its Elements.
- Resolve instructions in printed order, doing as much as possible. Inability to perform one instruction does not prohibit playing or using a Power on an otherwise legal target. Target restrictions are in its target bar, not implied by its text. You may even target a land where the effects accomplish nothing, but must actually attempt the text to count as using/targeting the Power.
- You may forego the whole Power, but cannot arbitrarily omit a possible mandatory instruction after starting. “Up to” allows zero. “Or” chooses between its adjoining clauses, not other separate text on the card. Choose the branch **before resolving either option**; you cannot start one to inspect its results and then switch to the other. [FAQ .9v5kcmx]
- Resolve the base effect and every met threshold in printed order **unless explicit timing text says otherwise**: “First” and “Before” can place a threshold instruction ahead of earlier-printed base instructions. A level saying **Instead** replaces previous effects rather than adding to them. You may treat yourself as having fewer Elements **for the whole Power**, consistently, rather than selecting individual thresholds to omit.
- Check Elements when a threshold is reached: newly gained Elements can enable later levels; losing Elements can prevent later levels, without changing completed effects. Apply a threshold changing Speed, Range or targeting when checking that attribute, before the ordinary effects: for example, Thunderspeaker's met Fast threshold permits using its Innate in Fast. Speed/Range/targeting modifiers are checked in time to use them before targeting, and an “or” choice is made before its branch resolves.
- Non-board-changing effects last for this turn only unless explicitly stated otherwise. Defend and action skips do not remain for future turns.

- **Initial Blight:** Exactly one extra Blight total at setup, with or without a card; never repeat this on flips. This and outcome timing above are substantive corrections to older rulebook wording. [Setup: one-more-blight-errata]
- **Range boosts:** Numeric Range boosts do not waive source/target restrictions or the requirement “one of your lands.” A Power still requiring your Sacred Site must have such an origin. General Power Range boosts affect Range values with a **printed Range arrow** in Powers **used by the Spirit receiving the bonus**, including effect-text arrows, subject to all restrictions. They do **not** increase the amount of another Range bonus: another boost cannot turn **Reaching Grasp**'s printed +2 into a larger bonus. They do not extend another Spirit's Powers merely because those Powers target the boosted Spirit. A bonus restricted to Powers does not extend Growth; Power Cards also resolve after normal Growth has finished. A special rule granting extra Range specifically for targeting lands with certain contents changes only the targeting Range box: **Shadows of the Dahan** does not extend effect-text Range arrows. [Core: special-rule-range-bonuses-to-targeting; official FAQ: [Range boosts](https://querki.net/raw/darker/spirit-island-faq/What-do-range-boosts-affect)] [Core: .3y28aqg, .7w4g8nq]
- **Internal Range origins:** A Range arrow inside a land-targeting Power's effects is measured from the **target land**, unless stated otherwise. In a Spirit-targeting Power's effects, measure from the Presence of the Spirit following that instruction (usually the target Spirit), unless the Power says otherwise. Apply the **Power user's** Range bonuses, even if another Spirit supplies the measurement origin. **Blazing Renewal** explicitly uses the Power user's Presence as its origin. Bonuses belonging only to the instructed Spirit do not extend someone else's Power. [Official FAQ: [internal Range](https://querki.net/raw/darker/spirit-island-faq/range-in-text-of-powers-that-target-spirits)]
- **Changing contents:** A single-land Power normally counts contents when used and fixes the effect then. Island-wide effects defined for a class of lands check current contents when relevant (for example, **Dahan on their Guard** counts Dahan when Damage occurs). **Encompassing Ward** follows the target Spirit's current Presence, rather than marking the lands occupied when it was used. An explicitly moving effect is an exception. [Core: do-island-wide-effects-check-land-contents-at-resolution, .7w4ganu]
- **Innates with only self-modification:** A level merely changing a Power's own Speed/Range is insufficient to count as using/targeting it; it must have some instruction with potential to change the game state, even if no actual change occurs. [Core: can-an-innate-power-that-only-changes-speed-or-range-be-targeted]
- **Repeat limits:** **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength** repeat Power **Cards**, not Innates. Powerstorm's threshold repeats up to three **different** cards. A Range/Speed change granted by a threshold carries to a Repeat even if that threshold is no longer met; it does not stack the same Range bonus again. [Core: .3y28aex, .7w4g8q9, Repeating-internal-range-boosts]
- **Triggered effects:** “After” effects resolve after the whole originating action, not after each instruction within a Power. A triggered effect cannot trigger itself, even indirectly. Separately repeated instances can trigger one another, but neither can recur within its own chain. **Vengeance of the Dead** uses this timing; its corrected base text grants 3 Fear and, after an effect destroys Towns/Cities/Dahan in target land, deals 1 Damage per such piece destroyed. Its threshold may send that Damage into adjacent lands, while the original target remains the land whose qualifying destruction triggers it. The triggered effect still belongs to the Spirit that used Vengeance: if Bringer used it, its later Damage follows To Dream a Thousand Deaths even when another Spirit's action caused the triggering destruction. - **Fear cards:** **Dahan Raid/Dahan Enheartened** deal the listed total Damage, not that Damage to each Invader. Updated Dahan Enheartened II/III: each player chooses a different land, Gathers up to 2 Dahan, then deals 1 Damage (II) or 1 per Dahan (III) if Dahan are present; gathering zero is allowed. **Trade Suffers III** only downgrades in a Coastal land, whether City→Town or Town→Explorer. **Overseas Trade Seem Safer II** cancels an entire Coastal Build that would build a City; it does not substitute a Town. A normal Town Build still happens. **Scapegoats II/III** is one action per land with Towns/Cities: II destroys 1 Explorer per Town and 2 per City; III destroys all Explorers, then 1 Town per City. grades.question: A Spirit plays two Power Cards and later Repeats one. For an effect counting Power Cards played, such as Boon of Vigor, is the count two or three? Does the Repeat consume another ordinary Card Play, and does it nevertheless count as a new Power use?

expected.answer: Two cards played: a Repeat does not play another Power Card and adds no card to that count. It nevertheless counts as a new Power use. It consumes no additional ordinary Card Play; any payment required by a Repeat permission is separate.

requested_parts: A Spirit plays two Power Cards and later Repeats one. For an effect counting Power Cards played, such as Boon of Vigor, is the count two or three?

observed.answer: Count 2 card plays, not 3; Repeat no Card Play but is another Power use.

evidence.text: A Repeat activates a Power's effects again; it is not a second card play and grants no additional printed card Elements. It **does** count as another Power use. For effects counting cards played (such as Boon of Vigor), a Repeat adds no card play; count the card's original play only. A repeated effect explicitly granting Elements grants those again. Recheck thresholds using your current Elements; they were not spent on the original, but may since have been lost.

Retain changes to the Power, including extra Range or changed speed. An ordinary Repeat uses the Power's **most recently assigned speed**: a Slow Power repeats in Slow even if its permission came from a Fast Power; a formerly Fast Power explicitly made Slow before repeating now repeats in Slow. An instruction to Repeat immediately instead follows that explicit timing, directly after the originating use. [FAQ repeating-powers-with-changed-speeds] You may postpone choosing which eligible card to repeat until you actually repeat it, and make different choices/targets then. For **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength**, the Spirit receives a once-this-turn option rather than a grant-time selection of cards: a card played later that turn may be selected while it remains in play, subject to the permission’s restrictions and cost. [FAQ timing-of-choosing-powers-for-once-this-turn-repeats] Gift of Strength imposes its printed card-cost eligibility ceiling but requires no additional Energy payment for the Repeat, so an eligible card may be repeated with no Energy left. - **Triggered effects:** “After” effects resolve after the whole originating action, not after each instruction within a Power. A triggered effect cannot trigger itself, even indirectly. Separately repeated instances can trigger one another, but neither can recur within its own chain. **Vengeance of the Dead** uses this timing; its corrected base text grants 3 Fear and, after an effect destroys Towns/Cities/Dahan in target land, deals 1 Damage per such piece destroyed. Its threshold may send that Damage into adjacent lands, while the original target remains the land whose qualifying destruction triggers it. The triggered effect still belongs to the Spirit that used Vengeance: if Bringer used it, its later Damage follows To Dream a Thousand Deaths even when another Spirit's action caused the triggering destruction. [Core: what-items-are-triggered-actions, .bu6oc8x, .7w4gdth, .7w4gdtj]

Updated Dahan Enheartened II/III: each player chooses a different land, Gathers up to 2 Dahan, then deals 1 Damage (II) or 1 per Dahan (III) if Dahan are present; gathering zero is allowed. **Trade Suffers III** only downgrades in a Coastal land, whether City→Town or Town→Explorer. **Overseas Trade Seem Safer II** cancels an entire Coastal Build that would build a City; it does not substitute a Town. A normal Town Build still happens. **Scapegoats II/III** is one action per land with Towns/Cities: II destroys 1 Explorer per Town and 2 per City; III destroys all Explorers, then 1 Town per City. [Core: scapegoats-action] [Core: .7w4g8rq, .7w4g8ra, .bu6ocpc, .7w4g8qr]

An unqualified “+N Damage” threshold adds total Damage at that step, not N to every previously damaged piece. Damage boosts still belong to the original Power when it counts what it destroyed. [Core: .9v5kavn, .7w4g8qc, .7w4g8p0, is-boosted-damage-from-the-same-source]

Fear from **To Dream a Thousand Deaths** counts; normal Fear for destroying Towns/Cities does not, even when a Power caused the destruction. [Original core card text]

Moving Dahan to their original land can count as Move if the Power permits. **Blazing Renewal** permits its target Spirit to add its destroyed Presence directly to one legal island land, not to tracks. Its threshold moves Defend 2 with each Dahan it Pushes, leaving the remaining Defend in the target. A later Power moving those Dahan does not carry that Defend. [Core: .9v5kfqd, .9v5kfr0, .bu6oc8n, .bu6ocxq]

River's special Wetland-site rule remains River's own. [Core: .9v5kfhb, .7w4gdab, .bu6oebp, where-do-spirit-targeting-powers-add-their-fear]

[Core: .9v5kehe, when-does-swiftness-of-lightning-happen, if-a-special-rule-cares-about-elements-when-does-it-check-your-element-total, .7w4gefg]

grades.question: A Spirit has met an unused Innate’s Element requirements but has no cards in hand, no Energy and no ordinary Card Plays left. Can it use that Innate at the proper speed, what Energy or Card Play cost does it ordinarily have, and is it automatically available every turn?

expected.answer: It may use the eligible Innate at its proper speed: unless explicitly specified otherwise it costs no Energy and no Card Play and is not a card played from hand. Innates are automatically available every turn when their requirements are met. Ordinary once-per-turn and targeting rules still apply.
source_refs: CORE p.14 Spirit panel item 9; p.16 Powers

requested_parts: A Spirit has met an unused Innate’s Element requirements but has no cards in hand, no Energy and no ordinary Card Plays left. Can it use that Innate at the proper speed, what Energy or Card Play cost does it ordinarily have, and is it automatically available every turn?
observed.answer: Yes, Innate available each turn if Elements met; ordinarily no Energy or Card Play cost.

evidence.text: An Innate is available each turn when its Element requirements are met; ordinarily it costs no Energy and uses no Card Play. Elements are **checked, never spent**. The same Elements can satisfy multiple Powers and thresholds. Gain a card's Elements as soon as it is played, whether or not its text is used, and lose them as soon as it leaves play.

Retain changes to the Power, including extra Range or changed speed. An ordinary Repeat uses the Power's **most recently assigned speed**: a Slow Power repeats in Slow even if its permission came from a Fast Power; a formerly Fast Power explicitly made Slow before repeating now repeats in Slow. An instruction to Repeat immediately instead follows that explicit timing, directly after the originating use. [FAQ repeating-powers-with-changed-speeds] You may postpone choosing which eligible card to repeat until you actually repeat it, and make different choices/targets then. For **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength**, the Spirit receives a once-this-turn option rather than a grant-time selection of cards: a card played later that turn may be selected while it remains in play, subject to the permission’s restrictions and cost. grades.question: Without an effect granting a Repeat or another use, may a Spirit pay a Power Card's printed Energy cost twice to use it twice in one turn? If a Slow Power is made Fast, may it be used once in Fast and again in Slow?

expected.answer: No to both. Ordinary Powers have one use per turn; paying again grants no second use. Making Slow Fast changes that use's timing, not its number: use it in Fast only, with no separate Slow-phase use. Additional uses require an explicit effect such as Repeat.

grades.question: For a standard game, how many balanced Island Boards are used and chosen, how are their initial Invaders, Dahan and Blight placed, and how are the Minor/Major decks and shared piece supplies prepared?

expected.answer: Randomly choose one balanced Island Board per Spirit and join them into the island. Populate every land according to its printed Invader, Dahan and Blight icons, taking setup Blight from the box rather than depleting the pool; setup Blight does not cascade or destroy Presence. Shuffle Minor and Major decks separately, each with its own shared discard space, and put Energy, Invaders and Dahan in shared supplies accessible to players.
source_refs: CORE p.6 Island and Supply; pp.13,15

requested_parts: For a standard game, how many balanced Island Boards are used and chosen, how are their initial Invaders, Dahan and Blight placed, and how are the Minor/Major decks and shared piece supplies prepared?
observed.answer: One random board per Spirit; balanced layout per player count. Populate all lands per printed icons. Shuffle Minor/Major decks separately with own discards; make Invader/Dahan/Energy supplies available; standard Invader deck stage prep separately.

evidence.text:
1. **Island:** Randomly choose one Island Board per Spirit and join the balanced sides into the island. For one Spirit use one board. For two, any fitting arrangement is legal; the rulebook illustrates bottom-to-bottom with Oceans facing opposite outer corners. For three use the triangular layout, and for four the two-row parallelogram layout illustrated in CORE pp.6–7. [FAQ .7w4g8pg] Populate every land with its printed Invader, Dahan and Blight setup icons. Setup Blight comes from the box, never the Blight pool, and does not cascade or destroy Presence.
2. **Invader deck:** Shuffle each stage separately. Remove one card of each stage unseen. Stack **3 Stage I cards on top, 4 Stage II below them, 5 Stage III at the bottom**. Put this 12-card deck in Explore.
3. **Fear:** Put **4 Fear markers per Spirit** in the Fear Pool. Shuffle the 15 Fear Cards and use 9 unseen: three cards, Terror II divider, three cards, Terror III divider, three cards, from top to bottom. Start at Terror I. Leave space for Earned Fear Cards and Fear discard.
4. **Blight:** Randomly select a Blight Card, Healthy Island side up; do not inspect its reverse. Put **2 Blight per Spirit plus exactly 1 additional Blight total** on it. This is the official initial-pool correction. The additional 1 is applied only at setup, never again on a card flip. Remaining box Blight is separate from this pool.
5. **Supply:** Shuffle Minor and Major decks separately, each with its own discard. Make Invaders, Dahan and Energy available to everyone.
6. **Spirits:** Each player takes one color's 13 Presence and reminder markers (any accidental extra disk is a spare, not additional Presence for play), a different Spirit panel, and that Spirit's four Unique cards as their starting hand. Each starts on a different Island Board and follows the back-of-panel setup exactly. Where several choices equally satisfy setup, choose freely; separate Presence-placement instructions may use the same land. Put remaining disks on the dashed spaces of both Presence tracks; the leftmost solid starting spaces remain uncovered. Starting boards do not restrict where a Spirit can act after setup.
7. **Initial Explore:** Reveal the top Invader card and Explore normally. Then put it face-up in **Build**. This Explore is the last part of setup; Ravage starts empty. The first actual turn begins with the Spirit Phase.

- **Initial Blight:** Exactly one extra Blight total at setup, with or without a card; never repeat this on flips. This and outcome timing above are substantive corrections to older rulebook wording. [Setup: one-more-blight-errata]
- **Range boosts:** Numeric Range boosts do not waive source/target restrictions or the requirement “one of your lands.” A Power still requiring your Sacred Site must have such an origin. General Power Range boosts affect Range values with a **printed Range arrow** in Powers **used by the Spirit receiving the bonus**, including effect-text arrows, subject to all restrictions. They do **not** increase the amount of another Range bonus: another boost cannot turn **Reaching Grasp**'s printed +2 into a larger bonus. They do not extend another Spirit's Powers merely because those Powers target the boosted Spirit. A bonus restricted to Powers does not extend Growth; Power Cards also resolve after normal Growth has finished. A special rule granting extra Range specifically for targeting lands with certain contents changes only the targeting Range box: **Shadows of the Dahan** does not extend effect-text Range arrows. [Core: special-rule-range-bonuses-to-targeting; official FAQ: [Range boosts](https://querki.net/raw/darker/spirit-island-faq/What-do-range-boosts-affect)] [Core: .3y28aqg, .7w4g8nq]
- **Internal Range origins:** A Range arrow inside a land-targeting Power's effects is measured from the **target land**, unless stated otherwise. In a Spirit-targeting Power's effects, measure from the Presence of the Spirit following that instruction (usually the target Spirit), unless the Power says otherwise. Apply the **Power user's** Range bonuses, even if another Spirit supplies the measurement origin. **Blazing Renewal** explicitly uses the Power user's Presence as its origin. Bonuses belonging only to the instructed Spirit do not extend someone else's Power. [Official FAQ: [internal Range](https://querki.net/raw/darker/spirit-island-faq/range-in-text-of-powers-that-target-spirits)]
- **Changing contents:** A single-land Power normally counts contents when used and fixes the effect then. Island-wide effects defined for a class of lands check current contents when relevant (for example, **Dahan on their Guard** counts Dahan when Damage occurs). **Encompassing Ward** follows the target Spirit's current Presence, rather than marking the lands occupied when it was used. An explicitly moving effect is an exception. [Core: do-island-wide-effects-check-land-contents-at-resolution, .7w4ganu]
- **Innates with only self-modification:** A level merely changing a Power's own Speed/Range is insufficient to count as using/targeting it; it must have some instruction with potential to change the game state, even if no actual change occurs. [Core: can-an-innate-power-that-only-changes-speed-or-range-be-targeted]
- **Repeat limits:** **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength** repeat Power **Cards**, not Innates. Powerstorm's threshold repeats up to three **different** cards. A Range/Speed change granted by a threshold carries to a Repeat even if that threshold is no longer met; it does not stack the same Range bonus again. [Core: .3y28aex, .7w4g8q9, Repeating-internal-range-boosts]
- **Triggered effects:** “After” effects resolve after the whole originating action, not after each instruction within a Power. A triggered effect cannot trigger itself, even indirectly. Separately repeated instances can trigger one another, but neither can recur within its own chain. **Vengeance of the Dead** uses this timing; its corrected base text grants 3 Fear and, after an effect destroys Towns/Cities/Dahan in target land, deals 1 Damage per such piece destroyed. Its threshold may send that Damage into adjacent lands, while the original target remains the land whose qualifying destruction triggers it. - **Fear cards:** **Dahan Raid/Dahan Enheartened** deal the listed total Damage, not that Damage to each Invader. evidence.text:
- **Initial Blight:** Exactly one extra Blight total at setup, with or without a card; never repeat this on flips. This and outcome timing above are substantive corrections to older rulebook wording. [Setup: one-more-blight-errata]
- **Range boosts:** Numeric Range boosts do not waive source/target restrictions or the requirement “one of your lands.” A Power still requiring your Sacred Site must have such an origin. General Power Range boosts affect Range values with a **printed Range arrow** in Powers **used by the Spirit receiving the bonus**, including effect-text arrows, subject to all restrictions. They do **not** increase the amount of another Range bonus: another boost cannot turn **Reaching Grasp**'s printed +2 into a larger bonus. They do not extend another Spirit's Powers merely because those Powers target the boosted Spirit. A bonus restricted to Powers does not extend Growth; Power Cards also resolve after normal Growth has finished. A special rule granting extra Range specifically for targeting lands with certain contents changes only the targeting Range box: **Shadows of the Dahan** does not extend effect-text Range arrows. [Core: special-rule-range-bonuses-to-targeting; official FAQ: [Range boosts](https://querki.net/raw/darker/spirit-island-faq/What-do-range-boosts-affect)] [Core: .3y28aqg, .7w4g8nq]
- **Internal Range origins:** A Range arrow inside a land-targeting Power's effects is measured from the **target land**, unless stated otherwise. In a Spirit-targeting Power's effects, measure from the Presence of the Spirit following that instruction (usually the target Spirit), unless the Power says otherwise. Apply the **Power user's** Range bonuses, even if another Spirit supplies the measurement origin. **Blazing Renewal** explicitly uses the Power user's Presence as its origin. Bonuses belonging only to the instructed Spirit do not extend someone else's Power. [Official FAQ: [internal Range](https://querki.net/raw/darker/spirit-island-faq/range-in-text-of-powers-that-target-spirits)]
- **Changing contents:** A single-land Power normally counts contents when used and fixes the effect then. Island-wide effects defined for a class of lands check current contents when relevant (for example, **Dahan on their Guard** counts Dahan when Damage occurs). **Encompassing Ward** follows the target Spirit's current Presence, rather than marking the lands occupied when it was used. An explicitly moving effect is an exception. [Core: do-island-wide-effects-check-land-contents-at-resolution, .7w4ganu]
- **Innates with only self-modification:** A level merely changing a Power's own Speed/Range is insufficient to count as using/targeting it; it must have some instruction with potential to change the game state, even if no actual change occurs. [Core: can-an-innate-power-that-only-changes-speed-or-range-be-targeted]
- **Repeat limits:** **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength** repeat Power **Cards**, not Innates. Powerstorm's threshold repeats up to three **different** cards. A Range/Speed change granted by a threshold carries to a Repeat even if that threshold is no longer met; it does not stack the same Range bonus again. [Core: .3y28aex, .7w4g8q9, Repeating-internal-range-boosts]
- **Triggered effects:** “After” effects resolve after the whole originating action, not after each instruction within a Power. A triggered effect cannot trigger itself, even indirectly. Separately repeated instances can trigger one another, but neither can recur within its own chain. **Vengeance of the Dead** uses this timing; its corrected base text grants 3 Fear and, after an effect destroys Towns/Cities/Dahan in target land, deals 1 Damage per such piece destroyed. Its threshold may send that Damage into adjacent lands, while the original target remains the land whose qualifying destruction triggers it. The triggered effect still belongs to the Spirit that used Vengeance: if Bringer used it, its later Damage follows To Dream a Thousand Deaths even when another Spirit's action caused the triggering destruction. [Core: what-items-are-triggered-actions, .bu6oc8x, .7w4gdth, .7w4gdtj]
- **Fear cards:** **Dahan Raid/Dahan Enheartened** deal the listed total Damage, not that Damage to each Invader. Updated Dahan Enheartened II/III: each player chooses a different land, Gathers up to 2 Dahan, then deals 1 Damage (II) or 1 per Dahan (III) if Dahan are present; gathering zero is allowed. **Trade Suffers III** only downgrades in a Coastal land, whether City→Town or Town→Explorer. **Overseas Trade Seem Safer II** cancels an entire Coastal Build that would build a City; it does not substitute a Town. A normal Town Build still happens. **Scapegoats II/III** is one action per land with Towns/Cities: II destroys 1 Explorer per Town and 2 per City; III destroys all Explorers, then 1 Town per City. [Core: scapegoats-action] [Core: .7w4g8rq, .7w4g8ra, .bu6ocpc, .7w4g8qr]

- **Spirit-targeting Powers:** When the target Spirit selects “one of their lands,” it chooses the land and does as much there as possible, even if another of its lands would permit more instructions. Thus **Mantle of Dread** may Push an Explorer from a land without a Town, and **Tidal Boon** may Push Dahan from a land without a Town. When Ocean uses Tidal Boon, Ocean may move Dahan pushed to its Ocean by that use to **any Coastal land**, including a nonadjacent one, instead of Drowning them. expected.answer: It need not keep its original target. The Spirit may choose any valid target by the ordinary Range and Target rules, either the original land or a different legal land. observed.answer: No specified Repeat target means any normally legal target, including original; ordinary Range/target rules apply.

- The **targeting Range box** gives the maximum land distance from **one of your Presence**. Range 0 requires your Presence in the target land. Origin icons may require your Sacred Site or Presence in a particular terrain.
- Target restrictions may specify terrain, Coastal/Inland, contents, or a Spirit. A slash between piece/terrain icons means either or both types, not an additional allowance for each.
- Unless explicitly different, use **one target land or Spirit, once per turn**. Multiple effects and all innate levels apply to that same target. You cannot pay twice for an ordinary card use or use an innate twice just by having twice its Elements.
- Resolve instructions in printed order, doing as much as possible. Inability to perform one instruction does not prohibit playing or using a Power on an otherwise legal target. Target restrictions are in its target bar, not implied by its text. You may even target a land where the effects accomplish nothing, but must actually attempt the text to count as using/targeting the Power.
- You may forego the whole Power, but cannot arbitrarily omit a possible mandatory instruction after starting. “Up to” allows zero. “Or” chooses between its adjoining clauses, not other separate text on the card. Choose the branch **before resolving either option**; you cannot start one to inspect its results and then switch to the other. [FAQ .9v5kcmx]
- Resolve the base effect and every met threshold in printed order **unless explicit timing text says otherwise**: “First” and “Before” can place a threshold instruction ahead of earlier-printed base instructions. A level saying **Instead** replaces previous effects rather than adding to them. You may treat yourself as having fewer Elements **for the whole Power**, consistently, rather than selecting individual thresholds to omit.
- Check Elements when a threshold is reached: newly gained Elements can enable later levels; losing Elements can prevent later levels, without changing completed effects. Apply a threshold changing Speed, Range or targeting when checking that attribute, before the ordinary effects: for example, Thunderspeaker's met Fast threshold permits using its Innate in Fast. Speed/Range/targeting modifiers are checked in time to use them before targeting, and an “or” choice is made before its branch resolves.
- Non-board-changing effects last for this turn only unless explicitly stated otherwise. Defend and action skips do not remain for future turns.

If a Repeat explicitly specifies its location, that location overrides the usual Range and target restrictions (e.g., “Repeat in an adjacent land” must be adjacent to the first target, and cannot be the original land). Otherwise choose any normally legal target, including the original. **Ignore Repeat instructions on a repeated Power:** repeats never chain into more repeat permissions. Other non-Repeat effects of that repeated Power still work.

General Power Range boosts affect Range values with a **printed Range arrow** in Powers **used by the Spirit receiving the bonus**, including effect-text arrows, subject to all restrictions. They do **not** increase the amount of another Range bonus: another boost cannot turn **Reaching Grasp**'s printed +2 into a larger bonus. They do not extend another Spirit's Powers merely because those Powers target the boosted Spirit. A bonus restricted to Powers does not extend Growth; Power Cards also resolve after normal Growth has finished. grades.question: Concealing Shadows has already resolved in Fast, so Dahan in its target land take no Damage from Ravaging Invaders this turn. That land now Ravages with one Town, one Explorer and two healthy Dahan, no Defend and no prior Blight. What happens to land and Dahan, how much counterattack Damage is available, and can it destroy both Invaders for how much Ravage-generated Fear?

expected.answer: The Invaders deal 3 Damage to land, adding one Blight; Concealing Shadows protects only Dahan and does not reduce land Damage. The Dahan take zero Damage and both survive healthy, then counterattack for 4 total Damage. They may destroy the Town (2 Health) and Explorer (1), with excess Damage unused, generating 1 Fear from the Town during this Ravage. The Power’s earlier printed Fear is separate from the requested Ravage-generated Fear.

requested_parts: Concealing Shadows has already resolved in Fast, so Dahan in its target land take no Damage from Ravaging Invaders this turn. That land now Ravages with one Town, one Explorer and two healthy Dahan, no Defend and no prior Blight. What happens to land and Dahan, how much counterattack Damage is available, and can it destroy both Invaders for how much Ravage-generated Fear?
observed.answer: Land takes 3 Damage -> one Blight. Concealing protects Dahan from Invader Ravage Damage, so zero Dahan Damage; both Dahan survive and deal 4 counterattack. They can destroy Town (2 damage) and Explorer (1) for 1 Fear from Town.

1. **Island:** Randomly choose one Island Board per Spirit and join the balanced sides into the island. For one Spirit use one board. For two, any fitting arrangement is legal; the rulebook illustrates bottom-to-bottom with Oceans facing opposite outer corners. For three use the triangular layout, and for four the two-row parallelogram layout illustrated in CORE pp.6–7. [FAQ .7w4g8pg] Populate every land with its printed Invader, Dahan and Blight setup icons. Setup Blight comes from the box, never the Blight pool, and does not cascade or destroy Presence.
2. **Invader deck:** Shuffle each stage separately. Remove one card of each stage unseen. Stack **3 Stage I cards on top, 4 Stage II below them, 5 Stage III at the bottom**. Put this 12-card deck in Explore.
3. **Fear:** Put **4 Fear markers per Spirit** in the Fear Pool. Shuffle the 15 Fear Cards and use 9 unseen: three cards, Terror II divider, three cards, Terror III divider, three cards, from top to bottom. Start at Terror I. Leave space for Earned Fear Cards and Fear discard.
4. **Blight:** Randomly select a Blight Card, Healthy Island side up; do not inspect its reverse. Put **2 Blight per Spirit plus exactly 1 additional Blight total** on it. This is the official initial-pool correction. The additional 1 is applied only at setup, never again on a card flip. Remaining box Blight is separate from this pool.
5. **Supply:** Shuffle Minor and Major decks separately, each with its own discard. Make Invaders, Dahan and Energy available to everyone.
6. **Spirits:** Each player takes one color's 13 Presence and reminder markers (any accidental extra disk is a spare, not additional Presence for play), a different Spirit panel, and that Spirit's four Unique cards as their starting hand. Each starts on a different Island Board and follows the back-of-panel setup exactly. Where several choices equally satisfy setup, choose freely; separate Presence-placement instructions may use the same land. 7. **Initial Explore:** Reveal the top Invader card and Explore normally. Then put it face-up in **Build**. This Explore is the last part of setup; Ravage starts empty. The first actual turn begins with the Spirit Phase.

**Defend N** reduces each occurrence of Invader Damage to both land and Dahan by N for this turn, to a minimum of zero. Multiple Defend effects add. grades.question: An effect explicitly adds two Blight simultaneously to one land containing two Presence from each of two Spirits. Counting only Presence destroyed in that land by this one addition, how many disks does each Spirit lose? Would adding one Blight there in each of two separate completed instructions destroy Presence once or twice, assuming each Spirit still has Presence there?

expected.answer: The simultaneous addition destroys one Presence from each Spirit, even though two Blight tokens are added. Two separate additions destroy one Presence per Spirit on each addition, hence two per Spirit if available. Cascades elsewhere are outside the requested count.

requested_parts: An effect explicitly adds two Blight simultaneously to one land containing two Presence from each of two Spirits. Counting only Presence destroyed in that land by this one addition, how many disks does each Spirit lose?
Would adding one Blight there in each of two separate completed instructions destroy Presence once or twice, assuming each Spirit still has Presence there?
observed.answer: One Presence from each Spirit for a single Blight addition regardless two Blight tokens (one per Spirit, so each loses 1). Two separate additions each destroy one per Spirit, so 2 each if remain.

evidence.text:
1. **Island:** Randomly choose one Island Board per Spirit and join the balanced sides into the island. For one Spirit use one board. For two, any fitting arrangement is legal; the rulebook illustrates bottom-to-bottom with Oceans facing opposite outer corners. For three use the triangular layout, and for four the two-row parallelogram layout illustrated in CORE pp.6–7. [FAQ .7w4g8pg] Populate every land with its printed Invader, Dahan and Blight setup icons. Setup Blight comes from the box, never the Blight pool, and does not cascade or destroy Presence.
2. **Invader deck:** Shuffle each stage separately. Remove one card of each stage unseen. Stack **3 Stage I cards on top, 4 Stage II below them, 5 Stage III at the bottom**. Put this 12-card deck in Explore.
3. **Fear:** Put **4 Fear markers per Spirit** in the Fear Pool. Shuffle the 15 Fear Cards and use 9 unseen: three cards, Terror II divider, three cards, Terror III divider, three cards, from top to bottom. Start at Terror I. Leave space for Earned Fear Cards and Fear discard.
4. **Blight:** Randomly select a Blight Card, Healthy Island side up; do not inspect its reverse. Put **2 Blight per Spirit plus exactly 1 additional Blight total** on it. This is the official initial-pool correction. The additional 1 is applied only at setup, never again on a card flip. Remaining box Blight is separate from this pool.
5. **Supply:** Shuffle Minor and Major decks separately, each with its own discard. Make Invaders, Dahan and Energy available to everyone.
6. **Spirits:** Each player takes one color's 13 Presence and reminder markers (any accidental extra disk is a spare, not additional Presence for play), a different Spirit panel, and that Spirit's four Unique cards as their starting hand. Each starts on a different Island Board and follows the back-of-panel setup exactly. Where several choices equally satisfy setup, choose freely; separate Presence-placement instructions may use the same land. Put remaining disks on the dashed spaces of both Presence tracks; the leftmost solid starting spaces remain uncovered. Starting boards do not restrict where a Spirit can act after setup.
7. **Initial Explore:** Reveal the top Invader card and Explore normally. Then put it face-up in **Build**. This Explore is the last part of setup; Ravage starts empty. The first actual turn begins with the Spirit Phase.

- The **targeting Range box** gives the maximum land distance from **one of your Presence**. Range 0 requires your Presence in the target land. Origin icons may require your Sacred Site or Presence in a particular terrain.
- Target restrictions may specify terrain, Coastal/Inland, contents, or a Spirit. A slash between piece/terrain icons means either or both types, not an additional allowance for each.
- Unless explicitly different, use **one target land or Spirit, once per turn**. Multiple effects and all innate levels apply to that same target. You cannot pay twice for an ordinary card use or use an innate twice just by having twice its Elements.
- Resolve instructions in printed order, doing as much as possible. Inability to perform one instruction does not prohibit playing or using a Power on an otherwise legal target. Target restrictions are in its target bar, not implied by its text. You may even target a land where the effects accomplish nothing, but must actually attempt the text to count as using/targeting the Power.
- You may forego the whole Power, but cannot arbitrarily omit a possible mandatory instruction after starting. “Up to” allows zero. “Or” chooses between its adjoining clauses, not other separate text on the card. Choose the branch **before resolving either option**; you cannot start one to inspect its results and then switch to the other. [FAQ .9v5kcmx]
- Resolve the base effect and every met threshold in printed order **unless explicit timing text says otherwise**: “First” and “Before” can place a threshold instruction ahead of earlier-printed base instructions. A level saying **Instead** replaces previous effects rather than adding to them. You may treat yourself as having fewer Elements **for the whole Power**, consistently, rather than selecting individual thresholds to omit.
- Check Elements when a threshold is reached: newly gained Elements can enable later levels; losing Elements can prevent later levels, without changing completed effects. Apply a threshold changing Speed, Range or targeting when checking that attribute, before the ordinary effects: for example, Thunderspeaker's met Fast threshold permits using its Innate in Fast. Speed/Range/targeting modifiers are checked in time to use them before targeting, and an “or” choice is made before its branch resolves.
- Non-board-changing effects last for this turn only unless explicitly stated otherwise. Defend and action skips do not remain for future turns.

- **Initial Blight:** Exactly one extra Blight total at setup, with or without a card; never repeat this on flips. This and outcome timing above are substantive corrections to older rulebook wording. [Setup: one-more-blight-errata]
- **Range boosts:** Numeric Range boosts do not waive source/target restrictions or the requirement “one of your lands.” A Power still requiring your Sacred Site must have such an origin. General Power Range boosts affect Range values with a **printed Range arrow** in Powers **used by the Spirit receiving the bonus**, including effect-text arrows, subject to all restrictions. They do **not** increase the amount of another Range bonus: another boost cannot turn **Reaching Grasp**'s printed +2 into a larger bonus. They do not extend another Spirit's Powers merely because those Powers target the boosted Spirit. A bonus restricted to Powers does not extend Growth; Power Cards also resolve after normal Growth has finished. A special rule granting extra Range specifically for targeting lands with certain contents changes only the targeting Range box: **Shadows of the Dahan** does not extend effect-text Range arrows. In a Spirit-targeting Power's effects, measure from the Presence of the Spirit following that instruction (usually the target Spirit), unless the Power says otherwise. Apply the **Power user's** Range bonuses, even if another Spirit supplies the measurement origin. **Blazing Renewal** explicitly uses the Power user's Presence as its origin. Bonuses belonging only to the instructed Spirit do not extend someone else's Power. grades.question: Concealing Shadows has resolved on a land. Later that turn, Poisoned Land resolves there and instructs the Spirit to destroy all Dahan. Does Concealing Shadows prevent those destructions? If Infinite Vitality's threshold had also resolved on that land this turn, would that threshold prevent them?

A protection explicitly limited to Dahan is different: **Concealing Shadows** makes Dahan take no Damage from Ravaging Invaders this turn, while land still takes its normal Damage and can Blight. Protected surviving Dahan then counterattack normally. It does not protect them from direct Destroy instructions or Damage from other sources. [FAQ .7w4g8nu; original card text]

General Power Range boosts affect Range values with a **printed Range arrow** in Powers **used by the Spirit receiving the bonus**, including effect-text arrows, subject to all restrictions. They do **not** increase the amount of another Range bonus: another boost cannot turn **Reaching Grasp**'s printed +2 into a larger bonus. They do not extend another Spirit's Powers merely because those Powers target the boosted Spirit. A bonus restricted to Powers does not extend Growth; Power Cards also resolve after normal Growth has finished. A special rule granting extra Range specifically for targeting lands with certain contents changes only the targeting Range box: **Shadows of the Dahan** does not extend effect-text Range arrows. [Core: special-rule-range-bonuses-to-targeting; official FAQ: [Range boosts](https://querki.net/raw/darker/spirit-island-faq/What-do-range-boosts-affect)] [Core: .3y28aqg, .7w4g8nq]

Apply the **Power user's** Range bonuses, even if another Spirit supplies the measurement origin. **Blazing Renewal** explicitly uses the Power user's Presence as its origin. Bonuses belonging only to the instructed Spirit do not extend someone else's Power. [Official FAQ: [internal Range](https://querki.net/raw/darker/spirit-island-faq/range-in-text-of-powers-that-target-spirits)]
- **Changing contents:** A single-land Power normally counts contents when used and fixes the effect then. Island-wide effects defined for a class of lands check current contents when relevant (for example, **Dahan on their Guard** counts Dahan when Damage occurs). **Encompassing Ward** follows the target Spirit's current Presence, rather than marking the lands occupied when it was used. - **Repeat limits:** **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength** repeat Power **Cards**, not Innates. Powerstorm's threshold repeats up to three **different** cards. A Range/Speed change granted by a threshold carries to a Repeat even if that threshold is no longer met; it does not stack the same Range bonus again. [Core: .3y28aex, .7w4g8q9, Repeating-internal-range-boosts]

evidence.text:
- The **targeting Range box** gives the maximum land distance from **one of your Presence**. Range 0 requires your Presence in the target land. Origin icons may require your Sacred Site or Presence in a particular terrain.
- Target restrictions may specify terrain, Coastal/Inland, contents, or a Spirit. A slash between piece/terrain icons means either or both types, not an additional allowance for each.
- Unless explicitly different, use **one target land or Spirit, once per turn**. Multiple effects and all innate levels apply to that same target. You cannot pay twice for an ordinary card use or use an innate twice just by having twice its Elements.
- Resolve instructions in printed order, doing as much as possible. Inability to perform one instruction does not prohibit playing or using a Power on an otherwise legal target. Target restrictions are in its target bar, not implied by its text. You may even target a land where the effects accomplish nothing, but must actually attempt the text to count as using/targeting the Power.
- You may forego the whole Power, but cannot arbitrarily omit a possible mandatory instruction after starting. “Up to” allows zero. “Or” chooses between its adjoining clauses, not other separate text on the card. Choose the branch **before resolving either option**; you cannot start one to inspect its results and then switch to the other. [FAQ .9v5kcmx]
- Resolve the base effect and every met threshold in printed order **unless explicit timing text says otherwise**: “First” and “Before” can place a threshold instruction ahead of earlier-printed base instructions. A level saying **Instead** replaces previous effects rather than adding to them. You may treat yourself as having fewer Elements **for the whole Power**, consistently, rather than selecting individual thresholds to omit.
- Check Elements when a threshold is reached: newly gained Elements can enable later levels; losing Elements can prevent later levels, without changing completed effects. Apply a threshold changing Speed, Range or targeting when checking that attribute, before the ordinary effects: for example, Thunderspeaker's met Fast threshold permits using its Innate in Fast. Speed/Range/targeting modifiers are checked in time to use them before targeting, and an “or” choice is made before its branch resolves.
- Non-board-changing effects last for this turn only unless explicitly stated otherwise. Defend and action skips do not remain for future turns.

**Defend N** reduces each occurrence of Invader Damage to both land and Dahan by N for this turn, to a minimum of zero. Multiple Defend effects add. It does not reduce Spirit Damage or make Dahan do less counterattack Damage. Land and Dahan receive the reduction separately, not by splitting a shared allowance. A protection explicitly limited to Dahan is different: **Concealing Shadows** makes Dahan take no Damage from Ravaging Invaders this turn, while land still takes its normal Damage and can Blight. Protected surviving Dahan then counterattack normally. It does not protect them from direct Destroy instructions or Damage from other sources. [FAQ .7w4g8nu; original card text]

- **Initial Blight:** Exactly one extra Blight total at setup, with or without a card; never repeat this on flips. This and outcome timing above are substantive corrections to older rulebook wording. [Setup: one-more-blight-errata]
- **Range boosts:** Numeric Range boosts do not waive source/target restrictions or the requirement “one of your lands.” A Power still requiring your Sacred Site must have such an origin. General Power Range boosts affect Range values with a **printed Range arrow** in Powers **used by the Spirit receiving the bonus**, including effect-text arrows, subject to all restrictions. They do **not** increase the amount of another Range bonus: another boost cannot turn **Reaching Grasp**'s printed +2 into a larger bonus. They do not extend another Spirit's Powers merely because those Powers target the boosted Spirit. A bonus restricted to Powers does not extend Growth; Power Cards also resolve after normal Growth has finished. A special rule granting extra Range specifically for targeting lands with certain contents changes only the targeting Range box: **Shadows of the Dahan** does not extend effect-text Range arrows. [Core: special-rule-range-bonuses-to-targeting; official FAQ: [Range boosts](https://querki.net/raw/darker/spirit-island-faq/What-do-range-boosts-affect)] [Core: .3y28aqg, .7w4g8nq]
- **Internal Range origins:** A Range arrow inside a land-targeting Power's effects is measured from the **target land**, unless stated otherwise. In a Spirit-targeting Power's effects, measure from the Presence of the Spirit following that instruction (usually the target Spirit), unless the Power says otherwise. Apply the **Power user's** Range bonuses, even if another Spirit supplies the measurement origin. **Blazing Renewal** explicitly uses the Power user's Presence as its origin. Bonuses belonging only to the instructed Spirit do not extend someone else's Power. [Official FAQ: [internal Range](https://querki.net/raw/darker/spirit-island-faq/range-in-text-of-powers-that-target-spirits)]
- **Changing contents:** A single-land Power normally counts contents when used and fixes the effect then. Island-wide effects defined for a class of lands check current contents when relevant (for example, **Dahan on their Guard** counts Dahan when Damage occurs). **Encompassing Ward** follows the target Spirit's current Presence, rather than marking the lands occupied when it was used. An explicitly moving effect is an exception. [Core: do-island-wide-effects-check-land-contents-at-resolution, .7w4ganu]
- **Innates with only self-modification:** A level merely changing a Power's own Speed/Range is insufficient to count as using/targeting it; it must have some instruction with potential to change the game state, even if no actual change occurs. [Core: can-an-innate-power-that-only-changes-speed-or-range-be-targeted]
- **Repeat limits:** **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength** repeat Power **Cards**, not Innates. Powerstorm's threshold repeats up to three **different** cards. A Range/Speed change granted by a threshold carries to a Repeat even if that threshold is no longer met; it does not stack the same Range bonus again. [Core: .3y28aex, .7w4g8q9, Repeating-internal-range-boosts]
- **Triggered effects:** “After” effects resolve after the whole originating action, not after each instruction within a Power. A triggered effect cannot trigger itself, even indirectly. Separately repeated instances can trigger one another, but neither can recur within its own chain. **Vengeance of the Dead** uses this timing; its corrected base text grants 3 Fear and, after an effect destroys Towns/Cities/Dahan in target land, deals 1 Damage per such piece destroyed. Its threshold may send that Damage into adjacent lands, while the original target remains the land whose qualifying destruction triggers it. The triggered effect still belongs to the Spirit that used Vengeance: if Bringer used it, its later Damage follows To Dream a Thousand Deaths even when another Spirit's action caused the triggering destruction. A normal Town Build still happens. **Scapegoats II/III** is one action per land with Towns/Cities: II destroys 1 Explorer per Town and 2 per City; III destroys all Explorers, then 1 Town per City. [Core: scapegoats-action] [Core: .7w4g8rq, .7w4g8ra, .bu6ocpc, .7w4g8qr]
- **Reading choices and Damage:** In **Crops Wither and Fade**, always gain 2 Fear before the City-or-Town replacement choice; “or” only divides adjacent clauses. **Veil the Night's Hunt** must put each point on a different Invader, wasting excess when there are fewer Invaders than Dahan. An unqualified “+N Damage” threshold adds total Damage at that step, not N to every previously damaged piece. Damage boosts still belong to the original Power when it counts what it destroyed. [Core: .9v5kavn, .7w4g8qc, .7w4g8p0, is-boosted-damage-from-the-same-source]
- **Core Power specifics:** **Song of Sanctity** is Slow, despite missing cost-circle ink in some printings. Its Explorer condition selects its effect: with Explorers, Push all of them; otherwise remove 1 Blight. This is not a free choice to remove Blight while Explorers remain. **Dissolve the Bonds of Kinship** line 3 Pushes all Explorers **to as many different lands as possible**, using every available legal destination up to the number of Explorers; its Invaders damaging each other do so simultaneously, **before** the Explorer Push as the threshold specifies. **Poisoned Land**'s threshold counts the Blight that its own earlier instruction added. **Tsunami**'s threshold adds Fear for each other Coastal land it affects. [Core: .7w4g9dg, .9v5kc31, .7w4ganc, .7w4g8q3, .7w4g8pc]
- **Dread Apparitions Fear sources:** While its effect is active, Power-generated Fear in its target land adds **Defend 1 per Fear**. Fear from **To Dream a Thousand Deaths** counts; normal Fear for destroying Towns/Cities does not, even when a Power caused the destruction. [Original core card text]
- **Location-dependent effects:** **Wrap in Wings of Sunlight** resolves its threshold’s **First, Gather up to 3 Dahan** before its base Move; those gathered Dahan may then move and allow the destination’s Defend. It grants no Defend if zero Dahan move: there is no moved-to land. Moving Dahan to their original land can count as Move if the Power permits. **Blazing Renewal** permits its target Spirit to add its destroyed Presence directly to one legal island land, not to tracks. Its printed “adds 2” is mandatory to the extent possible, using the Power user's Presence for its internal Range; it cannot deal threshold Damage with no destroyed Presence restored: “that land” refers to where it adds Presence. **The Trees and Stones Speak of War** deals 1 Damage per Dahan and grants Defend 2 per Dahan in its target land. Its threshold moves Defend 2 with each Dahan it Pushes, leaving the remaining Defend in the target. Only this Power's Defend 2 per pushed Dahan travels; separate Defend from another effect, such as Words of Warning, stays in its original land. A later Power moving those Dahan does not carry that Defend. [Core: .9v5kfqd, .9v5kfr0, .bu6oc8n, .bu6ocxq]
- **Protection:** **Infinite Vitality** replaces an attempted Blight addition by leaving that Blight in the active Blight Card/board pool. That prevented addition neither destroys Presence nor cascades. Its threshold protects Dahan from Damage/Destroy, not Remove/Replace. Its Blight protection does not make the land an illegal cascade destination. [Core: .bu6ocxx, .7w4g8q2]
- **Entwined Power:** Shared Presence applies only to targeting (Range/source/target boxes), not to text effects or counting “your lands.” One disk each can count as a Sacred Site for their Power targeting, but is not a real shared site for Fear Cards or other effects. River's special Wetland-site rule remains River's own. For its base card gains, the **target Spirit** first makes the normal draw-four/keep-one gain; the **using Spirit** then gains one of those same three unkept cards, without drawing another four. In solo, both gains come from that single four-card draw. The threshold also lets the using and target Spirits each independently gift the other one Power Card **from hand**, optionally; cards in play or personal discard cannot be gifted by it. The threshold gives 6 Energy in solo; each Major gained still needs a separate Forget. If a transferred Unique references a special effect defined by a Spirit's rule, such as Drown, that definition still applies; skip instructions requiring a personal track you do not have. [Core: .3y28auq, .3y28aeu, .7w4g9jw, .7w4gee7, .7w4g8p9]
- **Spirit-targeting Powers:** When the target Spirit selects “one of their lands,” it chooses the land and does as much there as possible, even if another of its lands would permit more instructions. Thus **Mantle of Dread** may Push an Explorer from a land without a Town, and **Tidal Boon** may Push Dahan from a land without a Town. Tidal Boon's “if Dahan are pushed” clause applies only to that Power's own Push. When Ocean uses Tidal Boon, Ocean may move Dahan pushed to its Ocean by that use to **any Coastal land**, including a nonadjacent one, instead of Drowning them. Ocean chooses; this alternative is optional. [Original core card text] Spirit-targeting Fear without a specified land has no particular land for **Dread Apparitions**. [Core: .9v5kfhb, .7w4gdab, .bu6oebp, where-do-spirit-targeting-powers-add-their-fear]

- **Lightning's Swift Strike:** During Fast, **Swiftness of Lightning** can make one Power Fast per current Air Element; Innates count as Powers too. Recheck current Elements each time; previous uses count against the current allowance. It grants one use at Fast, not an extra use in Slow. **Harbingers of the Lightning** generates its Fear in the target land. [Core: .9v5kehe, when-does-swiftness-of-lightning-happen, if-a-special-rule-cares-about-elements-when-does-it-check-your-element-total, .7w4gefg]
- **River Surges in Sunlight:** **River's Domain** makes its Wetland Presence a Sacred Site without increasing its disk count. When moving/affecting “a Sacred Site,” River may choose 1 or 2 actual Presence there as applicable. [Core: .9v5kfd7, .7w4gebd]
- **Shadows Flicker Like Flame:** Pay **Shadows of the Dahan**'s 1 Energy when using the Power, to ignore numeric Range to a land with Dahan. Source restrictions (such as needing a Sacred Site) and other target requirements remain. The payment's modification carries to a Repeat without paying that surcharge again; an explicit Repeat location still overrides normal targeting. For **Darkness Swallows the Unwary**, choosing lower Elements cannot select the second level without the first when both require the same Elements; if destroying Explorers under that level, first Gather an Explorer if able. [Core: .7w4g8pt, .7w4g8nq, .7w4g8r6, .bu6od0c]
- **A Spread of Rampant Green:** **Choke the Land with Green** is optional (some printings omit “may”). Each use skips just that Ravage or Build action and costs one of Green's Presence in its Sacred Site there. A later Build needs a fresh decision and another disk: starting with three, Green may skip the Ravage, retain a two-disk Sacred Site, then skip the Build and end with one disk. **Steady Regeneration**'s Healthy/Blighted test refers to the Blight Card, not Blight in the destination land. When adding Presence via Growth, Green may use destroyed disks instead of track disks even while disks remain on tracks: this is free while Healthy, or costs 1 Energy per destroyed disk while Blighted. This permission applies only to Growth; an ordinary Power needs its own explicit destroyed-Presence permission. Green's separate **Always** Range-2 Jungle/Wetland placement is additional to its one chosen Growth group, including when it chooses Reclaim/gain a Power. It still chooses only one of the optional groups. Growth instructions from multiple options can be ordered together, so a gained Power may inform the mandatory placement. Its explicit regeneration can use destroyed Presence; ordinary placement cannot. [Core: .9v5kc2v, .7w4g8r1, .bu6oegz, .7w4g8nv]
- **Thunderspeaker:** Presence may accompany each moved Dahan, including generic Move as well as Gather/Push; two Dahan can carry two Presence. **Sworn to Victory** triggers after an entire single-land Ravage for each Dahan destroyed there: destroy one of Thunderspeaker's Presence within Range 1 per Dahan, even if no Blight was added. Finish the Ravage, cascades and counterattack before this triggered loss. [Core: .bu6oc6l, .bu6oc73, .bu6ofsi]
- **Ocean's Hungry Grasp:** On a board with any of Ocean's Presence, the Ocean is a Coastal Wetland for **Powers and Blight**, not for normal Growth, Invader actions or Fear Cards. Powers and Special Rules can measure Range through it as a land. [Core: range-through-ocean] Powers can target it and move Invaders/Dahan into it; Blight can cascade into it. Other Spirits' Presence may end up there via a legal Power, including Thunderspeaker accompanying moved Dahan. You can measure Growth placement Range **from existing Ocean Presence**, although normal Growth cannot add to the Ocean just by treating it as a Coastal Wetland. The Growth group explicitly adding two Presence in **any Ocean** can place them in any board's Ocean, even a board where Ocean has no Presence, without a numeric Range requirement. Its other group's Range-1 **Coastal land** placement does not permit placing in the Ocean. Other placement must respect Ocean's land-type restriction unless expressly ignored (e.g., **Indomitable Claim** for Inland Presence). [Core: .bu6odcf, .7w4gef8, .9v5kf36, .9v5ka9o, .9v5kc4i, When-OHG-is-in-play-can-other-pieces-end-up-in-the-Ocean]
- **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. Humans cannot stay there between action trees: if Drowning fails, Push survivors to non-Ocean lands within that action. This is an actual Push and can trigger applicable movement effects, unlike later cleanup. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. Remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land afterward. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check. If no legal land exists return humans to supply as cleanup. [Core: .7w4g8qy, .9v5kbka, .7w4g8pb, .9v5ka9g, .7w4g8r4, .9v5kfqb, .9v5kfqs, .7w4gdtl]
- **Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares:** Its Powers' explicit Damage/Destroy cannot actually harm Invaders/Dahan or destroy anything except its own Presence. An explicit instruction to Damage or Destroy Dahan does nothing to those Dahan; skip that instruction and resolve the rest of the Power normally. For each Power use, evaluate what it would destroy if resolved normally: generate **0 Fear per Explorer, 2 per Town, 5 per City**, and Push the would-be-destroyed Explorers/Towns. No real Damage is marked, so different Powers or a Repeat cannot combine their hypothetical Damage; multiple instructions **within one Power** can. Existing real Damage from others helps its hypothetical destruction and remains unchanged afterward. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once. Repeats can “destroy” the same piece again for Fear. It does not get bonuses conditional on **actual** destruction (e.g., Mists of Oblivion or Vengeance of the Dead) from these pretend destructions. [Core: .7w4g7yx, .7w4g7yu, .7w4g8pj, .9v5kfh3, .9v5katc, .bu6oc6g]
- **Bringer's exceptions:** Fear Cards and Dahan counterattacks after its Defend deal real Damage, because they are not its Power's Damage. Bringer can Remove/Replace, add real Blight (destroying Presence normally), modify Invader actions or cause actual Ravage. Reducing Health or replacing a damaged piece with a lower-Health one can cause real destruction by core Health rules. If Bringer Pushes a “destroyed” Town into Ocean, Ocean's separate Drowning destroys it: **3 total Fear** (2 from Bringer, 1 from Ocean). **Spirits May Yet Dream** can flip any Fear Card, earned or anywhere in the deck. Its Element-granting level gives the target Spirit one Element of a type it already has at least one of; it cannot grant a currently absent Element type. [Core: .9v5ka92, .7w4g9jv, .9v5kf34, can-bringer-destroy-things-indirectly, .7w4g8pf, .7w4g8rd]
- **Call on Midnight's Dream:** “Forget this Power” refers to that card, not the newly gained card. Forgetting it to satisfy the gained Major's ordinary Forget requirement also satisfies its conditional; no second Forget is required. The forgotten card leaves play and cannot later be repeated via the normal once-this-turn permission. [Core: .9v5kc3z, .7w4gani, .9v5ka8w]

grades.question: Spirit A has an existing +2 bonus to its Power Ranges and uses Reaching Grasp, whose text grants target Spirit B +2 Range with all their Powers. Does A’s existing bonus increase the amount granted to +4, or does B receive +2? Does B’s Power-only bonus cover Innate Powers as well as Power Cards, and can it extend ordinary Growth placement?

expected.answer: The grant stays +2; Range boosts do not increase another Range boost. Reaching Grasp’s Power-only bonus applies to B’s Powers, including Innates and Power Cards, subject to the normal Range-arrow restrictions. It does not extend ordinary Growth, which is not a Power; Power Cards also resolve after normal Growth.
source_refs: Primary original Reaching Grasp face: card-scope-source/reaching_grasp.jpg

requested_parts: Spirit A has an existing +2 bonus to its Power Ranges and uses Reaching Grasp, whose text grants target Spirit B +2 Range with all their Powers. Does A’s existing bonus increase the amount granted to +4, or does B receive +2?
Does B’s Power-only bonus cover Innate Powers as well as Power Cards, and can it extend ordinary Growth placement?
observed.answer: A's +2 doesn't boost Reaching Grasp's fixed +2 grant; B receives +2. Applies B's all Powers including Innates, not Growth.

grades.question: For a Range arrow within a Power’s effect text, where is the origin for a land-targeting Power? Where is it for a Spirit-targeting Power used by Spirit A that instructs Spirit B to act? Which Spirit’s Range bonuses apply, and if that internal arrow is Range 1 with A having +2 and B having no bonus, what Range can it reach from whose Presence? How does Blazing Renewal’s explicit measurement origin differ?

expected.answer: For a land-targeting Power, measure the internal arrow from the target land unless otherwise specified. For a Spirit-targeting Power, normally measure from the Presence of the Spirit following the instruction, B here, unless the text says otherwise. Apply the bonuses of the Power user A, not B: the stated Range 1 becomes Range 3 from B’s Presence. Blazing Renewal explicitly measures from the Power user A’s Presence, even when B adds Presence; its explicit origin overrides the default.

evidence.text:
- The **targeting Range box** gives the maximum land distance from **one of your Presence**. Range 0 requires your Presence in the target land. Origin icons may require your Sacred Site or Presence in a particular terrain.
- Target restrictions may specify terrain, Coastal/Inland, contents, or a Spirit. A slash between piece/terrain icons means either or both types, not an additional allowance for each.
- Unless explicitly different, use **one target land or Spirit, once per turn**. Multiple effects and all innate levels apply to that same target. You cannot pay twice for an ordinary card use or use an innate twice just by having twice its Elements.
- Resolve instructions in printed order, doing as much as possible. Inability to perform one instruction does not prohibit playing or using a Power on an otherwise legal target. Target restrictions are in its target bar, not implied by its text. You may even target a land where the effects accomplish nothing, but must actually attempt the text to count as using/targeting the Power.
- You may forego the whole Power, but cannot arbitrarily omit a possible mandatory instruction after starting. “Up to” allows zero. “Or” chooses between its adjoining clauses, not other separate text on the card. Choose the branch **before resolving either option**; you cannot start one to inspect its results and then switch to the other. [FAQ .9v5kcmx]
- Resolve the base effect and every met threshold in printed order **unless explicit timing text says otherwise**: “First” and “Before” can place a threshold instruction ahead of earlier-printed base instructions. A level saying **Instead** replaces previous effects rather than adding to them. You may treat yourself as having fewer Elements **for the whole Power**, consistently, rather than selecting individual thresholds to omit.

Apply a threshold changing Speed, Range or targeting when checking that attribute, before the ordinary effects: for example, Thunderspeaker's met Fast threshold permits using its Innate in Fast. Speed/Range/targeting modifiers are checked in time to use them before targeting, and an “or” choice is made before its branch resolves.
- Non-board-changing effects last for this turn only unless explicitly stated otherwise. Defend and action skips do not remain for future turns.

- **Initial Blight:** Exactly one extra Blight total at setup, with or without a card; never repeat this on flips. This and outcome timing above are substantive corrections to older rulebook wording. [Setup: one-more-blight-errata]
- **Range boosts:** Numeric Range boosts do not waive source/target restrictions or the requirement “one of your lands.” A Power still requiring your Sacred Site must have such an origin. General Power Range boosts affect Range values with a **printed Range arrow** in Powers **used by the Spirit receiving the bonus**, including effect-text arrows, subject to all restrictions. They do **not** increase the amount of another Range bonus: another boost cannot turn **Reaching Grasp**'s printed +2 into a larger bonus. They do not extend another Spirit's Powers merely because those Powers target the boosted Spirit. A bonus restricted to Powers does not extend Growth; Power Cards also resolve after normal Growth has finished. A special rule granting extra Range specifically for targeting lands with certain contents changes only the targeting Range box: **Shadows of the Dahan** does not extend effect-text Range arrows. - **Internal Range origins:** A Range arrow inside a land-targeting Power's effects is measured from the **target land**, unless stated otherwise. In a Spirit-targeting Power's effects, measure from the Presence of the Spirit following that instruction (usually the target Spirit), unless the Power says otherwise. Apply the **Power user's** Range bonuses, even if another Spirit supplies the measurement origin. **Blazing Renewal** explicitly uses the Power user's Presence as its origin. [Official FAQ: [internal Range](https://querki.net/raw/darker/spirit-island-faq/range-in-text-of-powers-that-target-spirits)]
- **Changing contents:** A single-land Power normally counts contents when used and fixes the effect then. Island-wide effects defined for a class of lands check current contents when relevant (for example, **Dahan on their Guard** counts Dahan when Damage occurs). **Encompassing Ward** follows the target Spirit's current Presence, rather than marking the lands occupied when it was used. An explicitly moving effect is an exception. [Core: do-island-wide-effects-check-land-contents-at-resolution, .7w4ganu]
- **Innates with only self-modification:** A level merely changing a Power's own Speed/Range is insufficient to count as using/targeting it; it must have some instruction with potential to change the game state, even if no actual change occurs. [Core: can-an-innate-power-that-only-changes-speed-or-range-be-targeted]
- **Repeat limits:** **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength** repeat Power **Cards**, not Innates. Powerstorm's threshold repeats up to three **different** cards. Its threshold may send that Damage into adjacent lands, while the original target remains the land whose qualifying destruction triggers it. The triggered effect still belongs to the Spirit that used Vengeance: if Bringer used it, its later Damage follows To Dream a Thousand Deaths even when another Spirit's action caused the triggering destruction.
